CT CORONARY ANGIOGRAPHY

Clinical details: 64-year-old woman. Typical exertional angina. Type 2 diabetes, hypercholesterolaemia.

Technique:
Non-contrast prospectively gated calcium score acquisition followed by prospectively ECG-triggered CT coronary angiography.
Heart rate 63 bpm, sinus rhythm. Metoprolol 10 mg IV. GTN 800 micrograms sublingual.
Contrast: Omnipaque 350, 60 ml.
DLP 196 mGy.cm (estimated effective dose 5.1 mSv).

Calcium score:
Total Agatston score 212 (LMS 0, LAD 168, LCx 0, RCA 44). 86th percentile for age, sex and ethnicity (MESA).

Coronary arteries:
Right dominant.
Normal coronary origins and course.
LMS: no plaque.
LAD: calcified plaque in the mid segment with moderate (50-69%) stenosis. Diagonals unremarkable.
LCx: no plaque. Obtuse marginals unremarkable.
RCA: calcified plaque in the proximal segment with minimal (1-24%) stenosis.
Short superficial myocardial bridge of the distal LAD.

Non-coronary findings:
Cardiac chambers normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
The left atrial appendage is well opacified with no filling defect to suggest thrombus.
Ascending aorta 33 mm. Pulmonary trunk 25 mm.
Visualised lung bases unremarkable. No significant extracardiac findings.

Conclusion:
1. Moderate (50-69%) mid LAD stenosis in calcified plaque. Minimal proximal RCA disease. CAD-RADS 3/P2.
2. Functional assessment with stress perfusion cardiac MR is suggested if symptoms persist despite optimal medical therapy.
3. Optimisation of preventive therapy and risk factor modification is advised.
